players.product: AI server and switch system integration

quarterly_data.signal: The 10-K names Celestica's CCS segment customers as including Amazon Fulfillment Services, Meta Platforms, Google, Ciena, Dell Technologies, Hewlett-Packard Enterprise and IBM, and its ATS segment customers as including Applied Materials, LAM Research and Honeywell. Celestica generally enters into master supply agreements with customers that do not typically guarantee a particular level of business or fixed pricing; a majority require the customer to purchase unused inventory bought to fulfil its forecasted demand.

Capital expenditures were $201.2 million in 2025 (2024: $170.9 million; 2023: $125.1 million), mainly to expand manufacturing in Thailand, the U.S. and Malaysia and its design centers in support of AI/ML and HPS program growth; most 2025 and 2024 capex related to the CCS segment.

At December 31, 2025 Celestica reported binding purchase order obligations of $9,782.0 million ($9,495.3 million due in 2026). This includes $6,760.2 million of outstanding purchase orders not recognized on the balance sheet, a substantial portion of which are for standard inventory items procured for specific customers based on their purchase orders or forecasts, with those customers contractually liable for unconsumed material. Separately, capital expenditure commitments (open purchase orders) to third-party vendors were $257.7 million, primarily to support growth at certain sites driven by customer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: binding purchase order obligations $9,782.0 million (incl. $6,760.2 million off-balance-sheet purchase orders, mainly customer-specific inventory); capex commitments $257.7 million (Dec 31, 2025)
